credit_metrics.text: EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}} on revenue of {{revenue@FY2025}}, and operating profit declined by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}}.
Total debt was reduced by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}}, but gross leverage rose by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} as EBITDA fell.
Interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}}, still below the peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Cash generation weakened: FFO fell by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, taking FFO to debt down by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}, and free cash flow declined by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}}.
FCF to debt fell by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}, while capex intensity eased by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Liquidity rose by {{liquidity.change@FY2025}} to {{liquidity@FY2025}}, of which cash and cash-like investments of {{cash_like@FY2025}} were up {{cash_like.change@FY2025}}.
Undrawn committed facilities were stable at {{undrawn_facilities@FY2025}}, and liquidity to revenue rose by {{liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.

Customer prepayments grew: contract liabilities rose by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}}, while advance ticket cover fell by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}.
Towards the end of the year Finnair issued a bond to further strengthen its financial position and support the execution of strategic investments.

operating_performance.text: Passengers were broadly unchanged at {{passengers@FY2025}}, up {{passengers.change@FY2025}}, with the fleet stable at {{fleet@FY2025}} aircraft and an average age of {{fleet_age@FY2025}}.
The fuel share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2025}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{fuel_share_of_costs.peer_median@FY2025}}.
Costs related to environmental regulation increased significantly during the year, with greater use of sustainable aviation fuel and changes to the EU Emissions Trading System weighing on the result.
During the year Finnair purchased leased A321 aircraft, and all aircraft were in operative use at the balance sheet date.

peer_positioning.text: Finnair's clearest strength is cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, the highest of the network peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2025}}) against a median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Profitability and leverage are the weak spots: the EBITDA margin of {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} is the lowest of the group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2025}}) against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2025}}, and gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} is the highest ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

Net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} sits in the middle of the group, and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} is also in the middle, while FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} is the weakest of the peers ({{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

snapshot.text: Finnair, the Finnish network carrier, kept revenue broadly unchanged at {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025, a year in which prolonged industrial action in the first half weighed on the comparable operating result.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} as net debt was reduced by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is earnings quality: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, the weakest of the network peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2025}}), with FFO to debt down to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}.

watch_items.text: Earnings: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, below the peer median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2025}}, with industrial action in the first half weighing on the result.

Cash generation: FFO to debt fell by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}}, below the peer median of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}}, and FCF to debt dropped by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}.

Leverage: gross leverage rose by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@FY2025}}, so the reduction in net debt of {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} carried the net leverage improvement.

Costs and distributions: the fuel share of costs of {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{fuel_share_of_costs.peer_median@FY2025}}, and the Board proposes a return of capital to shareholders.
